title: fastpath: fast-path gating + precision toggle + safe-mode fallback for KV-batching correctness/perf
author: Ava Chen
description:
Context: Recent deployments exposed a correctness regression when using the fast-path kernels with aggressive KV-batching on long prefix scenarios. The fast-path assumes stable KV-cache hash layouts and mixed-precision kernel behavior; under some scheduling corner cases we observed mismatched KV indices and stale cache usage that produced token-level divergence (rare, but P0 customer-visible).

Goal: Introduce a minimal-surface gating and a runtime 'precision toggle' plus a cluster-level 'safe-mode' fallback that prioritizes correctness over peak throughput. This change keeps the fast-path available for the majority of workloads while ensuring safe fallbacks when invariant checks fail or when mixed-precision heuristics would risk correctness.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds fast-path gating hooks in the runtime scheduler to validate KV-cache layout/sequence invariants before selecting the fast kernel.
- Implements a per-request precision toggle: kernels can be asked to run in FP32 when invariants are borderline, falling back to FP16/INT8 when safe.
- Adds an opt-in cluster-wide 'safe-mode' flag (via config) that disables fast-path selection and forces conservative scheduling for affected nodes; safe-mode is exposed to ops for incident mitigation.
- Implements a lightweight runtime invariant check that verifies KV-cache offsets, sequence length monotonicity, and key-prefix consistency at batch boundaries (cheap checks; fast-path only enabled when they pass).
- Adds automated detection to downgrade to slow-path (reference kernel) with a diagnostic log and metrics when a mismatch is detected.
- Adds regression and e2e tests covering long-prefix KV-batching, mixed-precision path switching, and safe-mode flows.
- Updates docs and runbook: docs/notes/fastpath-safe-mode.md and ops runbook with rollback/playbook steps.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- Correctness-first: the invariant checks are intentionally conservative to avoid silent corruption. In the common case (short prefix, well-formed KV batches) we still hit the fast-path and see the same throughput improvements.
- Performance impact: in microbenchmarks the gating check adds ~0.4% CPU overhead on the scheduler path but prevents tail divergence cases. End-to-end throughput for language-generation workloads drops by ~3-6% in the worst-case (when safe-mode is enabled cluster-wide), but typical production workloads see <1.5% impact because safe-mode is rarely activated and the precision toggle keeps FP16 fast kernels available for compatible requests.
- Complexity: We keep the fast-path kernel implementations unchanged; the PR focuses on selection/gating and a thin precision wrapper. This reduces maintenance risk vs. rewriting kernels.

Testing and verification:
- Unit tests for invariant checks and precision toggle logic (CI).
- Integration tests: test/kv_batching/integration_test.py simulates interleaved long/short prefixes and validates output equality across fast/slow paths.
- Performance tests: perf-canary runs on benchmark lab (configs included). Numbers included in docs/notes/fastpath-safe-mode.md.
- Staged rollout: feature gated behind runtime config and Canary SST; ops can flip safe-mode remotely if problems are observed.

Rollback and mitigation:
- Revert the feature gate or enable cluster safe-mode to immediately force slow-path.
- Diagnostics include per-request trace id and KV-cache snapshot (limited sampling) to assist debugging.

Checklist:
- [x] Adds gating and precision toggle logic
- [x] Adds safe-mode config + ops runbook
- [x] Tests and perf numbers included
- [x] Docs updated

Related: ENG-4721 (regression triage), ENG-4803 (fast-path perf follow-ups).
